clue.text: I might be suffering and gripped by pain

indicators.note: being gripped by something means sitting inside it, so the word and goes within the word for pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they are in agony, clutched by pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I might be' only links; the definition is 'suffering' in the sense of putting up with something.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate or endure it, so enduring and suffering coincide.

clue.text: A girl's required; no rash could make her right

indicators.note: the letters could be made into something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl needs no rash to make her well.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so it stands for a girl by example.

clue.text: A fabled king with skill to hurt — not quite

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A legendary king has a talent for wounding, almost.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary king of Camelot.

clue.text: A kind of car to shun on motorway

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A car you'd avoid on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper car at a fairground is a dodgem.

clue.text: Not able to keep ice clear as the day

indicators.note: one piece keeps, or holds, the other inside

explanation.surface: It is impossible to keep the ice transparent by day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious and easily seen is noticeable.

clue.text: Boy-trap holds 14 lines from poet's brain

parts.note: a net is a trap for fish or birds

explanation.surface: A snare for a lad contains a fourteen-line verse dreamt up by a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic form of fourteen-line poem, composed by a poet.

clue.text: Past players' view: "Such skies may threaten rain"

parts.note: the cast are the players in a show

explanation.surface: A former company's actors forecast rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouded-over skies are overcast and look likely to rain.

clue.text: Ran up to bed with chopped ice — that fights pain

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read upwards

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone hurried to bed with crushed ice to ease the pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that dulls pain and induces sleep is a narcotic.

clue.text: Spread teat with glue — we call it education

indicators.note: spread about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Smearing a nipple with adhesive is passed off as schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is instruction or teaching.

clue.text: I don't eat mince — might be a cure for you!

indicators.note: to mince is to chop finely, so these letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vegetarian's refusal of minced meat is passed off as a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince' looks like the meat being refused, but it is the signal to rearrange I DON'T EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that counteracts a poison or illness is a cure.

clue.text: Hunter, a bishop who breaks plates in two

indicators.note: the bishop's letters break into the plates, splitting them in two

parts.note: plates of meat is rhyming slang for feet
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A hunting bishop smashes crockery into two pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plates' is Cockney rhyming slang: plates of meat means feet. 'breaks ... in two' says the bishop splits the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The ferret is a small animal kept to hunt rabbits and rats.

clue.text: Half envy couple, spoiled in luxury

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined and mixed up, so these letters are rearranged
half of the four-letter word envy is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A pampered pair, half envied, are ruined by their extravagant living.
explanation.walkthrough: EN from 'Half envy' joins COUPLE and 'spoiled' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Great wealth and lavish living is luxury.

clue.text: A place for teaching whales, collectively

definitions.meaning: an establishment where pupils are taught
a group of whales or fish swimming together

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an educational institution and the collective noun for a group of whales.

clue.text: New girl gets stuck with "dragnet restoration"

indicators.note: restoring rebuilds the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A new girl gets stuck restoring a fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-garde means innovative and new.

clue.text: Soliciting to make the painting squeal!

parts.note: to squeal and to sing both mean to inform on someone

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to make a picture shriek.
explanation.definitionFit: Going round asking for votes or custom is soliciting them.

clue.text: Row about score — "more grouchy", if you wish

indicators.note: the row goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: to etch is to score a surface

explanation.surface: A grumbler disputes a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy means irritable, so tetchier is more irritable.

clue.text: A children's game that calls for this tinned fish

definitions.meaning: a hide-and-seek game where seekers crowd into the hiding place
small fish sold packed in tins

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a hide-and-seek party game and a small tinned fish.

clue.text: A dig up round the Tate that's in a state

indicators.note: the reversed dig goes round the gallery's name
in a down clue, up means read upwards

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: An excavation around the Tate gallery leaves people worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a state means being upset and flustered.

clue.text: Longfellow's poem this girl won't conceal

definitions.meaning: an 1847 narrative poem by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
a girl's name, that of the poem's heroine

explanation.walkthrough: 'won't conceal' is loose linking: the girl is named openly as the poem's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Longfellow titled his narrative poem after its Acadian heroine, and the title is also a girl's name.

clue.text: Fetch up some wine at once and meditate

indicators.note: in a down clue, fetching up means bringing upwards, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: red is a kind of wine

explanation.surface: Bring up some wine straight away and then ponder.
explanation.definitionFit: To wonder is to ponder or meditate.

clue.text: Married when losing head and so did yearn

indicators.note: losing its head means dropping its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone longed to be married but lost their head.
explanation.definitionFit: Itched, as in itched to go, means longed or yearned.

clue.text: Cow left in steamship dirty looks will earn

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the steamship letters

explanation.surface: A cow left aboard a steamer gets dirty looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Scowls are angry, frowning looks.

clue.text: The army young — half dead with cats about

indicators.note: the word cats goes about, that is around, the other piece
half of the four-letter word dead is its first two letters

explanation.surface: The young recruits are half dead from cats all around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Young trainees in the armed forces are military cadets.

clue.text: Cogs ain't moving? I'm inclined to doubt

indicators.note: letters on the move are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A sceptic is unsure whether the gears are turning.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who doubts the existence of God, neither believing nor denying, is an agnostic.

clue.text: It's natural in pub and swallowed, side by side

parts.note: if you ate something you swallowed it

explanation.surface: Drinking and eating side by side in a pub comes naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality one is born with is inborn, or natural.

clue.text: Pitt, Irish playwright, wrote Portillo's guide

parts.note: Brad Pitt is the film actor
George Bernard Shaw was an Irish dramatist

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister and an Irish dramatist apparently penned a politician's guidebook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitt' suggests the Prime Minister but gives BRAD, from Brad Pitt. Michael Portillo, a former British politician, presents TV rail journeys guided by a Victorian railway guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Portillo's television rail series follows Bradshaw's Victorian railway guide.

clue.text: Disturbed desire to live in just one street

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unsettled urge to live on only one street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just one street' is loose padding, perhaps hinting at a side street.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live in it.

clue.text: In Western Isles the newly-weds he'll meet

explanation.surface: A man meets honeymooning women in Scotland's islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The island chain off north-west Scotland, also called the Western Isles.
